# 0.6.3 — Remaining CI diff failures

24 September 2026. Patch on **0.6.2**.

Upgrade if a CI diff plan still crashed after 0.6.2 with `encode`, `KeyError`, `Invalid object name`, or `list index out of range`. Each of those cases still exits `1`, with a sentence instead of the exception. `FULL` is unchanged.

## Install

```bash
pip install opentide==0.6.3
export OPENTIDE_REPO_ROOT=/path/to/detection-repo
opentide validate --strict
```

## Fixed

- A missing tip SHA names `CI_COMMIT_SHA`, `GITHUB_SHA`, or `BUILD_SOURCEVERSION` instead of `'NoneType' object has no attribute 'encode'` ([#339](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/339)).
- Azure `STAGING` without `SYSTEM_PULLREQUEST_SOURCEBRANCH` and `SYSTEM_PULLREQUEST_TARGETBRANCHNAME` names those variables. The check runs before `origin.fetch()`, so a checkout with no remote no longer dies with `No git repository was found at origin` ([#339](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/339)).
- A GitHub or Azure pull-request ref that is not on `origin` reports `Could not find git ref origin/<name>` instead of `Invalid object name` ([#339](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/339)).
- `DEBUG`, `MANUAL`, and `ALWAYS` under CI report `Deployment plan <NAME> is not a CI diff plan. Use STAGING, PRODUCTION, or FULL.` `ALWAYS` is no longer an alias of `FULL` ([#339](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/339)).
- A GitLab merged-result commit with one parent keeps `CI_COMMIT_SHA` and exits `0` when both SHAs are in the checkout, instead of `list index out of range` ([#339](https://github.com/OpenTideHQ/opentide/issues/339)).

## Verify

```bash
python -c "import opentide; print(opentide.__version__)"
opentide setup --yes --name "Tutorial Detections" --org "Example Corp" --platform sentinel --path /tmp/tutorial-detections
opentide --repo /tmp/tutorial-detections validate --strict
```

Expect `0.6.3`.
